join_order.notes: Drive from small seq_ids set; walk movie_keyword__keyword_id CSR to gather candidate movie_ids
Filter candidate movies by t.production_year > 2010 via direct array access on title.id (dense identity)
For each surviving movie, scan mi.info range via movie_info__movie_id offsets; break on first 'Bulgaria' match (existence)

data_structures.aggregation: scalar min over varlen (std::string_view tracked, materialize at end)

parallelism.notes: Driver set (seq_ids) is tiny (~200); candidate movies ~50k; final mi probes ~6k. Per-op work is small and dominated by random index/varlen access; threading overhead dominates.

execution_notes: Step 1: Scan keyword/keyword.off+.dat via memmem('sequel') to collect seq_ids (small).

Step 2: For each kid in seq_ids, walk movie_keyword__keyword_id CSR: lo=off[kid], hi=off[kid+1]; for each k_pos, mk_row=rowids[k_pos]; mv=movie_keyword/movie_id.bin[mk_row]; insert mv into candidate_movies set.
Step 3: For each mv in candidate_movies, check title/production_year.bin[mv] (title is dense identity, so id==row). Keep mv if y!=INT32_MIN && y>2010.

Step 4: For each surviving mv, range-scan movie_info via offsets[mv..mv+1]; for each r, length prefilter (off[r+1]-off[r]==8) then memcmp against 'Bulgaria'. On first hit, take t.title[mv] and update running MIN (lex compare). Break inner loop on hit (existence semantics).
Step 5: Output min title (or NULL if no rows).
